decisions.reason: As a safety-shoe line in the firm's core competence, it builds directly on existing design, certification, production, and channel knowledge, so management would be more likely to refine it than withdraw it.

The comfort insole remains close to the firm's footwear and fitting expertise, but as a supporting add-on beside other insole concepts it still carries some portfolio-rationalisation risk if customer pull or differentiation is not strong enough.
The ergonomic safety-shoe series is highly aligned with the firm's established protective-footwear knowledge and visible innovation direction, which makes continued improvement more likely than exit.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a specialised but related extension of the firm's protective-footwear capabilities, so they are likely to stay unless the niche market proves too small or costly to serve.

The moulded insole was presented as a flagship development and draws heavily on the firm's existing footwear, fit, and material know-how, so management would be very reluctant to drop it at this stage.
